note: Follow-up to the version 2 campaign (run with run_campaign.py --followup). Models and artifacts come from v2_models.json. Phases run in this order; each writes to its own folder under EAB_RUNS (default ~/eab-runs/v2-followup).

phases.name: triage
phases.why: Six canonical requests per step on the later release: does it load, do the prompts carry the tools, are the calls structured. Covers the 14 steps the stack decided under v0.8.0, three readable anchors, and the GPU path that v0.9.0 reports working on this board.

phases.name: v093
phases.why: The full version 2 protocol on every stack-decided step that the triage found readable, plus the three anchors, to measure release-to-release drift on configurations that were readable under v0.8.0.

phases.name: lengthsweep
phases.why: Under v0.9.3 the compiled Gemma-4-E4B-it receives the tools and answers in prose. Tool calling against prompt length, from one tool definition (about 900 tokens) to about 2,800 tokens, with compiled Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as a control for the padding.

phases.name: greedy
phases.why: Canonical suite x3 with top_k 1 on the release the report measured, on the llama.cpp configurations that varied most at temperature 0 (and one leader), and on one compiled bundle to check which sampler it applies.

phases.name: seed
phases.why: Canonical suite x3 with a seed other than the one the bundle's configuration declares: if the replies change, the bundle samples rather than decoding greedily.

phases.name: flat
phases.why: Canonical suite x3 with the flat schema (one tool per command, 16 tools offered), to check whether the nested schema's shape affects the scores, on two NPU paths, a CPU leader and the largest bundle.
